items.claim: The opening seam is carried by the English rendering of the row's onset verse, whose pointed bytes supply neither a vocative nor an imperative shape, while the row's 2 Hebrew splices both fall inside the unit rather than at either edge.
items.evidence: The onset verse reads הוֹצִ֥יא עַם עִוֵּ֖ר (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.8): the verb is pointed with hireq-yod, not the tsere shape the causative imperative of this root takes, and the verse carries no vocative and no second-person form, so the row's 'fresh addressee' is a construal of the rendering rather than a byte-visible addressee marker. The summons verse behind it opens נִקְבְּצ֣וּ (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.9), a suffix-conjugation form whose summons force likewise comes from the modal rendering. No per-token parsing layer is staged, so the form class is held rather than asserted -- but the row supplies no Hebrew at its own seam verse at all, its two byte-tier splices falling at oshb:Isa.43.10 and oshb:Isa.43.13, both interior. Stronger byte-internal evidence sat unused: אֲנִ֣י ה֔וּא at MT 43:10 and אֲנִ֣י ה֔וּא at MT 43:13 are BYTE-IDENTICAL, and that exact run stands at only three MT verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses across 1,291 MT verses at byte tier; 5 verses at accent-stripped tier), so two of the three bracket this very span as an inclusio; and the postpositive divine-utterance signature stands at MT 43:10 and MT 43:12 -- וְאַתֶּ֥ם עֵדַ֛י נְאֻם יְהוָ֖ה (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.12) -- the witness verdict the row cites only once (sweep: 2 verses in MT chs 42-45, 23 book-wide, skeleton tier). Parashah disclosure for the span is complete and correctly typed (setumah at MT 43:10 and MT 43:13, tier-3, single-witness), and no ketiv/qere or special-letter object falls in the span.

items.claim: Both edges of this two-verse unit rest on byte-verified divine speech frames, and its own address is set off by a four-fold plural-suffix chain, with the parashah layer corroborating at both edges under the correct type.
items.evidence: The onset frame is כֹּֽה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה גֹּאַלְכֶ֖ם קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.14) and the frame closing the unit off is כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הַנּוֹתֵ֥ן (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.16); both are the divine class, not the royal-messenger class, which is confined to the four narrative-chapter sites, so frame ownership is unambiguous here even though the row leaves the class unstated in its prose. Internal cohesion is tighter than the row argues: four second-person PLURAL suffixes fall inside two verses -- the redeemer noun of the onset frame and לְמַעַנְכֶ֞ם at MT 43:14 (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.14), then קְדֽוֹשְׁכֶ֑ם at MT 43:15 and מַלְכְּכֶֽם at MT 43:15 (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.15) -- against the singular address that runs both before and after this neighbourhood. The row also avoids the title trap correctly: the absolute title in the onset frame and the suffixed epithet at MT 43:15 are distinct objects and the row makes no count claim over them. Tier-3 parashah corroborates at both edges under the right type (setumah at MT 43:13 and MT 43:15, single-witness, never a driver), and the rival the row rejects is byte-answerable, since the following unit carries its own frame.
tier_citations: tier-3 parashah, single-witness: SAMEKH at MT 43:13 and MT 43:15

items.claim: The row's repeated form-class label is contradicted by the pointed bytes it rests on, and the participle chain it argues from is spliced at 1 of its 2 members.
items.evidence: The prose calls MT 43:18-19 an imperative turn and makes that label the ground of its own disclosed internal rival, but the bytes read אַֽל תִּזְכְּר֖וּ and אַל תִּתְבֹּנָֽנוּ (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.18) -- negation plus prefix-conjugation, the prohibitive pattern, which is not an imperative form; the verse the row pairs with it opens הִנְנִ֨י עֹשֶׂ֤ה חֲדָשָׁה֙ (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.19), which is not directive at all. Form-class labels carry the same discipline as digits, and no per-token parsing layer is staged, so the honest options are the byte-visible pattern or a stated functional reading; the row asserts neither. The participle claim is byte-true but incomplete: only the first member is spliced, while the second, הַמּוֹצִ֥יא at MT 43:17 (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.17), is what makes it a chain and is argued in prose without a form. The bounds themselves stand -- a fresh divine frame at byte tier at oshb:Isa.43.16 and the address shift at MT 43:22 -- and parashah disclosure for the span is complete and correctly typed (setumah at MT 43:21, tier-3, single-witness).
tier_citations: tier-3 parashah, single-witness: SAMEKH at MT 43:21

items.claim: The contrast the row uses to justify its opening seam is byte-false at the seam itself, and the signal that is byte-visible there -- a shift from plural to singular address -- goes unnamed.
items.evidence: The verse immediately preceding the row closes יָצַ֣רְתִּי לִ֔י (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.21), a first-person perfect with a first-person suffix on the noun that follows it, so the preceding material at the seam is first-person divine speech, not the 'third-person self-predication' the row asserts; the third-person description in that unit is confined to its 2 frame participles at MT 43:16-17, four verses back from the seam. What does stand at the seam is a number shift: הֲל֖וֹא תֵֽדָע֑וּהָ (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.19) and the prohibitive at MT 43:18 address a plural, while the row's own onset reads קָרָ֖אתָ יַֽעֲקֹ֑ב (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.22) with singular verbs continuing through MT 43:23-24 -- the strongest byte-visible ground available, and unused. The row's disclosed rival is also under-evidenced: the fresh self-declaration at MT 43:25 reads אָנֹכִ֨י אָנֹכִ֥י (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.25) and stands against אָנֹכִ֥י אָנֹכִ֖י at MT 43:11 (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.11) -- the two identical at ACCENT-STRIPPED tier, not byte (the accents differ), 2 verses in MT chs 42-45 -- which is exactly the voice-continuity evidence the row's decision to hold the lawsuit whole needs and does not cite. Parashah disclosure for the span is complete and correctly typed (setumah at MT 43:24 and MT 43:28, tier-3, single-witness), and no ketiv/qere object falls in the span.

items.claim: The divine-speech frame is attached to the wrong bytes: the clause the row labels the frame formula is the fear-not clause that follows it, and the frame itself sits one verse inside the row rather than at its onset.
items.evidence: MT 44:2 runs כֹּה אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֥ה עֹשֶׂ֛ךָ וְיֹצֶרְךָ֥ מִבֶּ֖טֶן יַעְזְרֶ֑ךָּ and only then אַל תִּירָא֙ עַבְדִּ֣י יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב (byte tier, oshb:Isa.44.2): the clause the row calls the frame formula is the fear-not formula, which the frame introduces; the frame's owner is also left unnamed in the prose, though these bytes are the divine class and not the royal-messenger class of the narrative chapters. The row's onset verse carries no frame at all -- its byte-tier splice at oshb:Isa.44.1 is an imperative plus vocative, a defensible tier-1 onset, but the row never discloses that the speech frame falls INSIDE the unit rather than opening it, which is the fact its rival most needs answered. Two precisions on the servant naming: at MT 44:1 the servant noun attaches to Jacob alone, יַעֲקֹ֣ב עַבְדִּ֑י, while Israel is named as chosen, וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּחַ֥רְתִּי בֽוֹ (byte tier, oshb:Isa.44.1); the parallel term in the next verse is וִישֻׁר֖וּן at MT 44:2 (byte tier, oshb:Isa.44.2), not Israel -- the row's 'Jacob and Israel NAMED as servant' is true of the two verses taken together, not of the verse it splices. Finally the echo the row claims to the earlier fear-not oracle is byte-true but unspliced and untiered: both openings carry וְעַתָּ֞ה (MT 43:1) and וְעַתָּ֥ה (MT 44:1), which match at ACCENT-STRIPPED tier, not byte. Parashah disclosure for the span is complete and correctly typed (petuchah at MT 44:5, tier-3, single-witness), and no ketiv/qere object falls in the span.

tier-3 parashah, single-witness: PE at MT 44:5

items.claim: The row's 2 Hebrew-dependent claims -- the closing rock epithet and the witness catchword across its own seam -- are each argued with 0 Hebrew splices, in two classes this book flags for byte discipline.
items.evidence: The epithet is וְאֵ֥ין צ֖וּר at MT 44:8 (byte tier, oshb:Isa.44.8), a member of the rock / adversary / Tyre homograph family, so the claim has to name the form and the object; the row names neither and quotes no Hebrew for it. The cross-seam catchword the row does disclose -- good practice, and the disclosure is the right move -- is not the identity the untiered phrasing implies: וְאַתֶּ֣ם עֵדָ֑י at MT 44:8 against וְעֵדֵיהֶ֣ם at MT 44:9 (byte tier at each ref) share the root and differ in every affix. The chain is also wider than the adjacent pair: the second-person witness formula stands at MT 43:10, MT 43:12 and MT 44:8 (sweep: 3 verses in MT chs 42-45, skeleton tier) and the third-person counter-witnesses at MT 43:9, יִתְּנ֤וּ עֵֽדֵיהֶם֙ (byte tier, oshb:Isa.43.9), and MT 44:9 -- a bracket over the whole neighbourhood, of which the row discloses one link. The bounds stand: the onset frame at MT 44:6 is byte-verified divine, the self-declaration splice reaches byte tier, and no parashah, ketiv/qere or special-letter object falls inside the span, so the single cited mark before the span is the whole of what is owed.

items.claim: The register shift the row makes its primary ground is unsupported in the pointed bytes and contradicted by the one staged layout witness, and the root that opens the row is the frame word of the units on both sides -- a byte-true cross-seam pull left undisclosed.
items.evidence: The row argues its onset from a 'prose-inside-poetry register shift', but the pointed extract carries no prose/poetry layer at all, and the English witness sets EVERY verse of Isa.44.9-Isa.44.20 in poetry lines (12 of 12 verses, 47 lines) -- layout that is tier-4 in either direction and cannot carry a boundary ground. The row's other stated ground is byte-true and sufficient on its own: יֹֽצְרֵי פֶ֤סֶל (byte tier, oshb:Isa.44.9) opens a third-person description, and no first-person DIVINE form occurs anywhere in the span (the only first-person forms sit inside the idol-maker's quoted speech at MT 44:16, MT 44:17 and MT 44:19), against the first-person declarations of the preceding unit. What is undisclosed is that the forming root of the row's own onset word is the frame word on both sides -- יָצַ֣רְתִּי לִ֔י at MT 43:21, וְיֹצֶרְךָ֥ מִבֶּ֖טֶן at MT 44:2, יְצַרְתִּ֤יךָ עֶֽבֶד לִי֙ at MT 44:21 (byte tier at each ref) -- and recurs inside the satire at יָצַ֥ר (MT 44:10) and יִצְּרֵ֑הוּ (MT 44:12): sweep 9 verses in MT chs 43-44, defective spelling in all 9 with the plene spelling attested 0 times in that window (skeleton tier). That is a byte-true device straddling this row's closing seam and arguing continuity unless disclosed. Two disclosure items: the ketiv/qere citation at MT 44:24 lies four verses beyond the span and is justified in the prose by another row's use of the field rather than verse-anchored; and the row's own onset verse is the only verse in the book whose LETTER BYTES carry extraordinary upper points -- וְעֵדֵיהֶ֣ם הֵׄ֗מָּׄהׄ at MT 44:9, three upper-dot codepoints (sweep: 1 verse across 1,291 MT verses; single-witness; a letter-byte fact, not a seg, and no small- or large-letter claim is made or implied) -- undisclosed in the very verse the row splices from. Credit where due: the in-span ketiv/qere at MT 44:17, the small nun at MT 44:14 and the setumah at MT 44:20 are each disclosed with digit, object, single-witness naming and no position claim.

items.claim: The row discloses 1 cross-seam tie, an untiered recurrence whose two forms match at no tier above the root, and its mark disclosure stops at the edge before the span while a petuchah -- the rarer of the layer's 2 mark types (41 PE against 168 SAMEKH over 209 marked MT verses) -- stands at the verse it argues as its closing boundary.
items.evidence: The redemption tie is כִּ֥י גְאַלְתִּֽיךָ at MT 44:22 against כִּֽי גָאַ֤ל at MT 44:23 (byte tier at each ref): same root, different conjugations, identical at ROOT level only and not at byte, accent-stripped or skeleton tier -- so the row's unqualified 'recurs' overstates it, where the honest citation is a root-tier catchword (the redemption family stands in 6 verses of MT chs 42-45, skeleton tier). On the marks, the row cites the setumah before its span at MT 44:20 but not the petuchah at MT 44:23: the parashah layer brackets MT 44:21-23 as one section, which is tier-3 single-witness corroboration running toward the row's own disclosed rival. The layer is tier-3 corroboration rather than a driver and its absence carries no counterevidential weight, so the cut can stand -- but engaging the mark at one edge while omitting the mark at the other, on the exact question the row raises, is asymmetric. A second tie runs backward and is unnamed: מָחִ֤יתִי כָעָב֙ פְּשָׁעֶ֔יךָ at MT 44:22 answers מֹחֶ֥ה פְשָׁעֶ֖יךָ at MT 43:25 (byte tier at each ref; sweep: 2 verses in MT chs 42-45, skeleton tier), which is the blotting language the row's own summary leans on. The servant naming is byte-correct and properly kept out of the held question: כִּ֣י עַבְדִּי אָ֑תָּה and יְצַרְתִּ֤יךָ עֶֽבֶד לִי֙ (byte tier, oshb:Isa.44.21) name Israel outright, so this belongs to the named-referent class and not to the unnamed-figure zones, and the row decides no referent.
